svg.text: On another pane: above, below, left or right of it (the two then
share its room), or its middle, which swaps the two. On the
section’s own edge: the pane takes that whole side. Panes are
never stacked as tabs: a hidden table is the opposite of the
point. Past the window’s edge nothing lands; floating is Pop
The button at the end of the command bar. Locked, the grips go
and nothing drags. A heading’s own menu has Move (left, right,
up, down) so no pointer is needed; a divider takes the arrow
takes the room the other two gave up
Fold: a pane shrinks to its heading where it stands and its
neighbours take the room; the same mark opens it. There is no
"hidden": a pane is always on screen as itself, its heading, or its
stand-in. Floating: Pop out sends the card over the game and
leaves the stand-in, which keeps the pane’s place (and can itself
be moved). Dock, Bring back and Dock all return the card to it.
320 wide, 132 tall: a heading, column headings and three rows.
Under 700 wide the panes fall into one column in reading order
and the page scrolls, as today. The arrangement is kept and
Damage, Healing and Compare each keep their own. View
